naming: A name is listed once. A method name that ends in an extension (Q, CS, XT, Z, ZZ, U, IB, W...) is the same method written with one more word: each method lists the extensions that exist for it and the names of its forms. A method that only forwards to another is that method under another name (also_written on the method), and a class with nothing in it but its parent is that class under another name (also_named): ask for the main name.

extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained
chains on the next, more specific type of object (the Q ladder)
chains on the most specific type of object (the Q ladder)
chains on a copy, so the original object stays unchanged
returns the result as an object of the requested type
takes the position to start from (StartingAt)
the extended form: more parameters than the base method
yet another extension: a further extended form, after XT
includes the position in what it returns
selects by a condition, with the expressive keywords (@NextItem, @PreviousItem...)
takes a direction, forward or backward (Directional)
takes a function (the condition or the update is given as a function); the forms document also uses F for the future form, which defers the action
works on a collection of items instead of one (the plural form)
takes exceptions, what to leave out (the exceptional form)

discipline.about: How to think and write Softanza, read before the names: seven steps of thought, fourteen rules of writing. Page: https://mayouni.github.io/stzsite/en/way.html

steps.step: Define the problem in natural terms and take its keywords out.
steps.sample: Uppercasing and then spacifying 'softanza', so we get 'S O F T A N Z A'

steps.step: Select the object the problem is about.
Act on the positions, or call the verb whose name says the act.
Celebrate and repeat: the answer is read under its arrow, and the chain keeps its history.

rules.rule: A value is lifted to its object by Q(), or by its typed lifter when the type is the point.
A scene is a brace block on one object, and the questions are asked inside it.
Every printed line carries its answer under #-->; a multi-line answer is drawn as the console shows it.
A parameter is named, and the name reads as English.
A chain mirrors the order of thought: one step per line, the dot at the end.
The form of the verb says what happens: Remove acts, Removed gives a copy, RemoveQ hands the object back.
Suffixes and prefixes are small and each means one thing: CS, XT, FF, W, Z, ZZ.
A function has alternatives for the way a person says it.
Precision over generality, when it costs nothing: NumberOfChars() over Size(); ContainsBoth, ContainsAll, ContainsSome.
Code travels inside an argument as a small string, with @item, @char, @1 as placeholders.
Small literal languages live in strings.
A function may be named in any human language.
A comment speaks before the code, in the teacher's voice; a test block is framed by /*--- title, pr() and pf().

A tree that only a C++ adapter can read serves the first and not the second, so it goes out as JSON -- inspectable, diffable, assertable in CI, and the shape an adapter of any language can consume.

methods.name: ReadAgents

methods.name: AgentQ

methods.name: CiteRefusals

methods.name: Rescan
methods.description: AND ONE THING IT CANNOT DO, REPORTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: a changed .pia file is re-read, because it is data. A changed .ring file is NOT re-evaluated, because Haro cannot unload a function and re-loading it is a C22 redefinition that takes the library down. So the old code keeps running and this rescan says so, as a refusal carrying the file's name. A reload that quietly kept stale code would be the worst of the three available outcomes.

methods.name: MountOn
methods.description: Declare() is called for each even though a declared agent answers CoverageStatement() and ReversibilityClass() for itself: a Haro agent may answer only one of them, and the host's declared table is the fallback the engine gate reads. Saying it twice costs nothing; saying it never is a refusal at RunFor() time.

(A raw SetNodeProperty still bypasses it -- the audit stays the backstop -- but the composition API refuses.) This is the guardrail moving from audit to gate. TRUE when granting pcCap to pcActor would keep the graph sound w.r.t. no-llm-effectful (a queryable form of the constraint).

methods.name: Explain
methods.description: a readable verdict for the composition

methods.name: SetReactor
methods.description: Share another host's loop (e.g. an stzAppServer's) instead of owning one -- "the agent host is the same host".

methods.name: SetRetirementGovernance
methods.description: The governance whose decommission contract gates Retire(). NOTE: the stored @oGov is a COPY (governance is pure Haro lists -- no shared engine handle), so the decommission contract MUST be declared and fulfilled THROUGH THE HOST (below), which mutates this live copy. Fulfilling on the caller's original would leave the host's copy stale (the Haro aliasing doctrine).

methods.name: DeclareDecommission
methods.description: Declare an agent's decommission obligations (retirement is earned only once all are fulfilled).

methods.name: FulfillObligation
methods.description: Fulfill one obligation (mutates the host's live governance copy).

methods.name: Supervise
methods.description: supervision ----------------------------------------------------- Register an agent to be ticked every nTickMs. The agent must be fully configured (skills, governance) BEFORE this call.

methods.name: SuperviseOnEvent
methods.description: EVENT-DRIVEN supervision (R5 reactor-runtime): tick the agent once per EVENT emitted on pcChannel (the engine event bus, stzEventBus), not on a timer. The perceive-decide-act loop becomes a true event loop -- the agent reacts to what happens, when it happens. Past events are NOT replayed (the baseline is the channel's current count at registration).

methods.name: ChannelOf
methods.description: The channel an agent is event-supervised on ("" if timer-supervised).

methods.name: NameAt
methods.description: The nth supervised agent's NAME -- enumeration for an observer (the appserver's /agents surface) that must not hold the agent itself.

methods.name: AgentQ
methods.description: The live supervised agent (reach it here, not via a stale ref).

methods.name: UseAgentsFrom
methods.description: AND THE REFUSALS ARE NOT SWALLOWED. AgentLoadRefusals() carries every file the folder would not admit, in the unified finding shape, and CiteAgentLoadRefusals() prints them. A host that mounted three agents out of five and said nothing is the shape this exists to prevent.

methods.name: RescanAgents
methods.description: Returns [ :added, :changed, :removed ] -- the file names that moved.

methods.name: Declare
methods.description: the engine loop (Zig owns the tick) ----------------------------- Declare an agent's COVERAGE STATEMENT and REVERSIBILITY CLASS -- what law 18 obliges before anything schedules it. Needed only for agents that do not answer CoverageStatement() / ReversibilityClass() themselves; the host asks the agent first.

methods.name: SetPriority
methods.description: Higher runs first in a pass. Ties break on registration order, so the order is total and reproducible whether or not priorities are set.

methods.name: UseEngineLoop
methods.description: Adopt the Zig loop as this host's pump. Agents already supervised are registered now, so the call order does not matter -- and a refusal raises HERE, carrying the engine's own diagnostic.

methods.name: EngineLoopWhy
methods.description: The engine's last refusal, verbatim. A refusal names its code, its subject and what to do -- do not paraphrase it.

methods.name: EngineSlotOf
methods.description: The engine slot an agent occupies (-1 when the Haro pump is driving).

methods.name: TickDue
methods.description: the perceive-act runtime --------------------------------------- Tick every ACTIVE, non-retired agent whose interval has elapsed: run ONE Cycle() (perceive-decide-act) through the live index. Returns the number of skill-firings verified this pass.

methods.name: RunFor
methods.description: Drive the loop for nMs, ticking due agents. The inter-tick wait is a REAL libuv timer awaited on the engine loop thread (falls back to a Haro sleep only when no reactor DLL is present -- LAW 2).

methods.name: RunToQuiet
methods.description: Run until every supervised agent reaches fixpoint (a full pass with zero firings) or the cap is hit -- the cascade at host level.

methods.name: Cancel
methods.description: cancellation + governed decommission --------------------------- Stop ticking an agent WITHOUT retiring it (reversible pause).

methods.name: SetActionBudget
methods.description: One agent acting in a loop floods everything downstream of it -- the cascading failure. A budget caps the ACTIONS (skill firings: what causes effects) an agent may take in a sliding window. An agent that exceeds it is QUARANTINED, not merely slowed: a runaway is a containment event, it stays stopped until an effectful actor releases it, and the reason says how far over it went. Both pumps account.

methods.name: ActionBudgetOf
methods.description: [ :max, :windowMs, :acts ] -- the acts counted in the current window

methods.name: Quarantine
methods.description: Between a pause and a retirement: the agent stops being run, with the REASON kept, and it stays stopped -- Resume() refuses while it is quarantined. Only Release(), by an effectful, non-sandboxed actor, lifts it. A Cancel is an operator's pause; a quarantine is a containment act.

methods.name: QuarantineOf
methods.description: [ :reason, :at ] or [] when the agent is not quarantined

methods.name: Retire
methods.description: DECOMMISSION (R4b): retirement is EARNED. When a governance is wired, the agent may retire ONLY once every declared obligation is fulfilled (MayRetire). A retired agent stops ticking permanently. Returns TRUE on retirement, FALSE (with Why()) on refusal.

methods.name: Shutdown
methods.description: teardown

methods.name: Learn
methods.description: A learned fact carries its PROVENANCE: which agent learned it (:source = "agent:<name>") and when (:learnedat, epoch ms). It used to carry nothing, so a memory read back could not say where a belief came from. No :confidence is invented -- nobody stated one; LearnXT takes the caller's own.

methods.name: ProvenanceOf
methods.description: Where a fact came from -- the provenance recorded when it was learned.

methods.name: Restore
methods.description: Read a saved memory back, provenance included. Returns the merge report [ :merged, :refused ]. (Not "Load": a Haro keyword.)

methods.name: Apply
methods.description: run only when the precondition holds; VERIFY the result before reporting success. Returns [ :ran, :verified, :why ].

methods.name: Id
methods.description: at construction, not at the first write

methods.name: SetActor
methods.description: Stamp the twin's actor so every rehearsed operation carries WHO proposed it -- the plan's narration then reads as a history with authors, not a list of anonymous changes.

methods.name: CreateFile
methods.description: rehearsal verbs: every one reaches the live twin THROUGH the -- table index, never through a copy

methods.name: Exists
methods.description: free inspection (reads the TWIN, not disk)

methods.name: WasDeleted
methods.description: read-through: twin first, tombstones second, disk last --------- Did the rehearsal remove this path? Only asked when the twin does not hold it -- a path deleted and then re-created is simply held.

methods.name: GenerateUpdatePlan
methods.description: the ONE export toward reality ---------------------------------- The rehearsal as a governed crossing artifact: narrated, ranked, re-validated, rejectable per step, committed under scope + capability + governance by whoever holds the executor's authority.

methods.name: AuthorizationHeader
methods.description: "Bearer <key>" -- governed (needs the real key), so for an effectful actor.

methods.name: AddThing
methods.description: == DOMAIN (Being) ======================================================= AddThing() performs the act and returns NOTHING; AddThingQ() performs it and hands back the app, so the block  AddThingQ(:X) { Has(...) Owns(:Y) } runs the app's OWN Has/IsTrue/Owns/Of on the current-thing cursor. (The core law: a plain name acts, the Q chains -- exactly as stzList does with AddItem() / AddItemQ().)

methods.name: AddFlow
methods.description: == LIFE - BEHAVIOR (Becoming) =========================================== When() returns This: the brace  { Require(:x)  Then( Keep(:Y) ) } runs app methods against the current-flow cursor.

methods.name: AddGoal
methods.description: == LIFE - PURPOSE (Becoming) ============================================ AddGoal() returns This; the brace assigns the goal-cursor ATTRIBUTES (Means/ReachedBy/Within/Respecting), flushed into the record by BraceEnd() when the brace closes.

methods.name: Goal
methods.description: THE DATA FORM (the house rule: a plain name returns DATA, the Q form returns the OBJECT). A goal as a plain record -- nothing to chain on.

methods.name: GoalName
methods.description: just the goal's NAME -- said precisely, since that is all it returns

methods.name: Pursue
methods.description: THE REAL PURSUIT: compile the goal's Means into an stzGraphGoal (a wanted graph state), measure the GAP on the live world graph, and turn each gap instance into a proposal through the matching Whenever/Propose reaction (or a bare :attend proposal when no reaction declares the way).

methods.name: SetBody
methods.description: == BODY (embodiment) ==================================================== SetBody() returns This; the brace assigns the body-cursor attributes (Graph_/Files/Keep_ -- note: the DSL keywords Graph and Keep collide with the Graph() accessor and the Keep(thing) flow verb, so the ATTRIBUTES carry a trailing underscore and BraceEnd reads whichever was written).

methods.name: Body
methods.description: the body as DATA (the Q form above returns the object)

methods.name: Surfaces
methods.description: THE DECLARATIONS, AS DATA. Anything outside (stzPlatform harvesting a world, a generator, a doc tool) asks through these -- it never reaches into the @attributes. AddReaches([...]) DECLARES the surfaces; Surfaces() reports them.

methods.name: Things
methods.description: [ [ thingName, [fields] ], ... ]

methods.name: Live
methods.description: == ANIMATION ============================================================ Live() wires the world's reactions into a running reactive system and does a first Pulse() so the live world already reflects what its Whenever/Propose rules imply. Continuous/temporal firing rides the R5 stzAgentHost runtime (supervise the world, tick Pulse()).

methods.name: Pulse
methods.description: PULSE: evaluate every reaction against the live world. A reaction 'Whenever :Thing ... Propose :Other' fires for each INSTANCE of Thing that lacks an <other>-labeled relation -- producing one proposal per gap (the same structural gap the goal machinery measures). Idempotent: a proposal already standing is not duplicated, and once the world Relate()s the instance the proposal clears on the next pulse. Returns proposals added.

methods.name: React
methods.description: React to an EVENT on one instance: pulse just that instance's reactions. Returns proposals added.

methods.name: Explain
methods.description: == PRESENCE (emergent) -- make the world visible ========================

methods.name: Start
methods.description: Materialise every dataset of the model as a real sqlite table (seeded with the model's rows), expose each for REST CRUD, and bind the host. nPortNum 0 = ephemeral. After this, the state is LIVE: it no longer lives in the model, it lives in the database the parts share.

methods.name: StartOn
methods.description: LEAVING THE LOOPBACK REQUIRES A KEY. On 127.0.0.1 the callers are this machine; on a real interface they are whoever can route to the port, and an unauthenticated MBaaS floor would take a POST from any of them. So a non-loopback bind without SetSigningKey() is REFUSED here rather than quietly exposed -- governed by construction, not by a later audit finding.

methods.name: BindHost
methods.description: The interface this backend is bound to (host mode).

methods.name: Serve
methods.description: Serve the backend to whoever connects, for nMs. This is what a HOSTING process runs after Start(): the loop that answers remote parts. (A local backend never needs it -- it pumps one event per crossing instead.)

methods.name: ConnectTo
methods.description: Attach to a backend ALREADY RUNNING somewhere else. No database and no server are created here -- this object becomes a pure client, and every part-scoped call below goes over the wire instead of over the loopback.

methods.name: SetSigningKey
methods.description: The shared secret that authenticates the crossing. Set it on BOTH sides: the HOST uses it to require a signature, the CLIENT to produce one. It is the same secret, so this one call serves both roles -- which is also why a real deployment must deliver it out of band (env, vault, stzSecretStore), never in the model file or the command line.

methods.name: LastStatus
methods.description: The HTTP status of the last crossing, either mode (0 = it never completed). 401 here means the far side refused the signature.

methods.name: IsReachable
methods.description: Is the far backend actually answering? (stzAppServer serves /health with no route declared, so this needs nothing from the model.)

methods.name: SpawnRemote
methods.description: Launch this model as a backend PROCESS of its own and return its endpoint. The child gets the serialised model + port + TTL on its command line, and self-terminates when the TTL expires (so a forgotten host cannot outlive the run). The spawning reactor is owned by THIS object, so the child's lifetime is tied to something the caller holds.

methods.name: SpawnRemoteOn
methods.description: The secret is handed over in the ENVIRONMENT (STZ_BACKEND_SECRET), not in argv -- see _GenerateHostScript.

methods.name: RemoteLaunchCommands
methods.description: THE SECRET IS NEVER IN THE COMMAND. argv is world-readable in the remote process table, so the launch line only NAMES the environment variable; the value must already be in the remote environment (deploy it from a vault or stzSecretStore out of band). A backend that leaks its own key while starting has authenticated nothing.

Returns [ rows, total, topDish, topRev ].

methods.name: Start
methods.description: launching the fleet

methods.name: WaitReady
methods.description: Poll every worker's /health until it answers 200 (workers need a moment to load stzBase + bind). Returns the number now ready.

methods.name: Route
methods.description: routing: RETRY-WITH-FAILOVER + per-worker CIRCUIT BREAKER ----------- Proxy to a healthy worker of pcTag. On a failed attempt (transport error or non-2xx), FAIL OVER to the next healthy worker, up to SetMaxTries. A worker that fails SetCircuitBreaker consecutive times has its circuit OPENED (skipped for the cooldown, then half-open). A success resets/closes its circuit. Path is SSRF/CRLF-validated first.

methods.name: TelemetryQ
methods.description: observability (latency percentiles + trace ids)

methods.name: LastTraceId
methods.description: The trace id assigned to the most recent Route (correlates the front host's record with the worker's _trace on the wire).

methods.name: LatencyP50
methods.description: Tail-aware latency for a facet (ms; the engine histogram bucket bound).

methods.name: RecentTraces
methods.description: The last n request records: [ id, facet, endpoint, status, durMs, attempts ].

methods.name: LimiterQ
methods.description: rate limiting (front-door admission)

methods.name: RateLimitedCount
methods.description: How many requests this facet has shed for exceeding its rate limit.

methods.name: TokensAvailable
methods.description: Tokens left in a facet's bucket (-1 = unlimited / no limit configured).

methods.name: FleetSize
methods.description: introspection

methods.name: ClassifierQ
methods.description: R8.2 smart routing (classify -> route) ----------------------------- A request classifier bound to THIS cluster's facet catalog (created lazily, after facets are declared).

methods.name: RouteRequest
methods.description: Classify a request to a facet (R8.2), then proxy it to a worker of that facet (R8.3). Returns the response body; "" (with negative RouteLastStatus) when the request is undecidable or has no worker.

methods.name: HealthCheck
methods.description: R8.4 health + elastic scale (the supervision surface) -------------- Re-probe every worker's /health and refresh its ready flag. A worker that stops answering (crashed, exited its TTL) flips to NOT ready. Returns the number ready now.

methods.name: DeadCount
methods.description: Workers that were launched but are not answering (crashed / expired).

methods.name: ScaleUp
methods.description: Add ONE worker of a profile (elastic scale-up). Spawns a new process on a fresh port; call WaitReady()/HealthCheck() to see it come up. Returns the new port.

methods.name: ScaleDown
methods.description: GRACEFUL drain-down: mark one ready worker of a profile DRAINING -- routing stops immediately (it finishes in-flight work), and the process self-exits on its TTL. Returns the drained port, or 0 if there is nothing to drain. (Forced kill of a hung worker is a small future engine add; drain is the graceful path.)

methods.name: RestartDead
methods.description: Respawn every dead worker in place (health-driven self-healing). Returns the number restarted.

methods.name: ForceKill
methods.description: forced kill + orphan cleanup (the forceful sibling of drain) -------- Force-kill EVERY spawned worker of a facet (SIGKILL). The forceful counterpart to ScaleDown's graceful drain: use it on a WEDGED worker that neither answers health nor self-exits on its TTL. Marks each not ready and returns how many were actually killed. External workers (RegisterExternalWorker, jobId 0) are NOT ours to kill and are skipped.

methods.name: KilledCount
methods.description: Total workers force-killed over the cluster's life (a hung-worker / orphan-cleanup signal for the health console).

methods.name: FleetMetrics
methods.description: A per-profile metrics snapshot the supervisor reads (REAL counts).

methods.name: Stop
methods.description: teardown ----------------------------------------------------------- R8.3: workers self-terminate on their TTL. Graceful drain / kill / health-restart / autoscale is R8.4 (stzAgentHost supervision).

methods.description: Bind the HTTP listener. nPortNum 0 = ephemeral (see Port()). Raises on bind failure -- no silent half-started server.

methods.name: StartTls
methods.description: Serve over TLS: the reactor terminates TLS per connection (server cert cCertPath + key cKeyPath) BELOW the router, so every handler runs on the DECRYPTED request and responses are encrypted transparently -- the routing/handler code is byte-for-byte identical to plain Start(). A non-empty cCaPath enables client-cert checks; bRequireClient = TRUE demands a valid client cert (mutual TLS). Same bind semantics as Start.

methods.name: ServeOne
methods.description: Drain events until ONE data event (an HTTP request or a raw chunk) has been handled, or nTimeoutMs elapses. Returns TRUE if work was done. Accept/closed events are drained silently along the way.

methods.name: RunFor
methods.description: With agents hosted, the serve slice is BOUNDED: ServeOne(nLeft) would otherwise park on the socket for the whole remaining time whenever no request arrives, and the agents -- which live on this same loop -- would never tick. So we serve for at most @nAgentSliceMs, then tick whatever is due, and repeat. Requests and perceive-decide-act interleave on ONE loop.

methods.name: Run
methods.description: Serve forever (until the process is killed or Stop() is called from a handler). The documented blocking entry point.

methods.name: Observe
methods.description: Observe this server with a perf monitor (perf P3). From this call on, every request records its response time R into the timer 'http.request.ms', its arrival into the counter 'http.requests' (throughput X = its measured rate), and 5xx outcomes into 'http.errors'; GET /metrics serves the monitor's Prometheus exposition, and /health widens with the process senses. The monitor's watched senses (memory/cpu) are ticked by the serve loop at the monitor's own cadence -- a served app samples itself.

methods.description: routing interface

methods.name: ObserveRoutes
methods.description: Per-route observation (perf P8): Observe() PLUS a timer FAMILY 'http.route.ms' labeled [method, route, class] -- one child per route the traffic actually exercises, each with its own percentiles ('class' is the status class: 2xx/4xx/5xx). Cardinality rides the family's bound: unruly path spaces land in the overflow child instead of exploding the registry.

For a view shared with the caller (and durability), give the stzAuth a stzAuthDbStore: its sqlite is an engine handle, so the server's copy reads and writes the SAME database -- a login through HTTP is then visible to the caller's object, and vice versa.

methods.description: WHY EVERYTHING GOES THROUGH THE SERVER. Haro copies objects on `=`, so the host stored here is the server's own copy: a caller who kept the original would watch a snapshot that never ticks. That is why the supervision and read methods below DELEGATE instead of handing the host out -- the same cure stzAgentHost itself applies to its agents, and stzSuperApp to its governance. Reach the live host only through these.

methods.description: how long a new session lives, in seconds (0 = no expiry). Existing sessions keep the TTL they were issued with.

methods.name: SetIdleTTL
methods.description: idle timeout: a session dies if untouched for this many seconds (0 = off). Every successful validation slides the window (touches last-seen).

methods.name: SetMailPort
methods.description: passwordless config (mail port + magic-link) -------------------- bind the mail PORT passwordless flows send through -- a stzMailSandbox in dev (captured + assertable), your SMTP adapter at deploy. Any object with Send(to, subject, body) works.

methods.name: SetMagicLinkBaseUrl
methods.description: the app URL a magic link points at; the token is appended as ?token=... (or &token=... if the URL already has a query). "" -> a softanza:// URI.

methods.name: SetPasswordlessTTL
methods.description: how long a magic link / email-OTP stays valid (seconds).

methods.name: SetMaxAttempts
methods.description: brute-force lockout config

methods.name: Register
methods.description: the credential store -------------------------------------------- register a user with a password -- stores ONLY the salted hash.

methods.name: RegisterPasswordless
methods.description: register an account with NO usable password -- reachable only through a passwordless factor (magic-link / email-OTP). The stored hash is of a random value nobody holds, so Login can never succeed for it.

methods.name: ChangePassword
methods.description: change a password (the current one must be presented). TRUE on success.

methods.name: Unregister
methods.description: remove a user (and end any of their sessions).

methods.name: Authenticate
methods.description: MIGRATION: a hash stored before Argon2id (PBKDF2 "salt:hash") is still accepted, and on a SUCCESSFUL check it is replaced by an Argon2id hash of the password just proven -- the only moment the plaintext is in hand. So old accounts upgrade themselves, one login at a time, with no reset.

methods.name: Login
methods.description: authenticate AND, on success, open a session -> returns an opaque token ("" on failure OR lockout -- indistinguishable, so it leaks nothing).

methods.name: LoginAt
methods.description: deterministic form (explicit 'now') for tests.

methods.name: LoginWith
methods.description: same, capturing the DEVICE CONTEXT (ip + user-agent) so the session can be listed and revoked per device.

methods.name: LoginTwoFactor
methods.description: Password AND second factor in one call. For a user WITHOUT 2FA the code is ignored (password alone opens the session), so an app may always route login through here. For a 2FA user, a valid TOTP (or one-time recovery) code is required. Returns a session token, or "" on any failure / lockout.

methods.name: LoginTwoFactorWithAt
methods.signature: LoginTwoFactorWithAt(pcUser, pcPassword, pcCode, pcIp, pcUserAgent, pnNow)

methods.name: UserOfSession
methods.description: the user behind a live session token, or "" if unknown / ended / EXPIRED (checked against the wall clock).

methods.name: UserOfSessionAt
methods.description: same, against an explicit 'now' (epoch seconds) -- deterministic for tests. Checks BOTH the absolute expiry and (when enabled) the idle window, and slides the idle window by touching last-seen on a valid access.

methods.name: SessionToken
methods.description: the session as a stzToken (its expiry, its kind), or NULL if unknown -- reconstructed from the stored token + expiry.

methods.name: SessionExpiresAt
methods.description: the epoch-seconds a session expires at (0 = never), or -1 if unknown.

methods.name: PurgeExpiredAt
methods.description: drop expired sessions (housekeeping) -> the number pruned. Prunes BOTH absolute-expired and (when idle timeout is on) idle-expired sessions.

methods.name: RevokeSession
methods.description: revoke ONE session (per-device "sign out this device"). Alias of Logout, named for the device-management flow.

methods.name: RevokeAllSessions
methods.description: end EVERY session for a user without removing the account ("log out everywhere") -- distinct from Unregister.

methods.name: SessionsOf
methods.description: the "your devices" surface + fixation defense ------------------- every live session of a user, as public descriptors -- the data a "your active devices" view lists (token to revoke by, plus when/where/what). [ [ :token, :user, :created, :ip, :userAgent, :expires, :lastSeen ], ... ]

methods.name: SessionInfo
methods.description: one session's public descriptor, or [] if unknown.

methods.name: RotateSession
methods.description: ROTATE a session's token (session-fixation defense): after a privilege change -- 2FA, password change, elevation -- issue a NEW token for the same user + device, void the OLD one, and return the new token ("" if invalid). The pre-elevation token can no longer be replayed.

methods.name: HasTotp
methods.description: A user may add an authenticator-app second factor. Enrollment is TWO steps so a mis-scanned secret can never lock the user out: EnableTotp issues a secret stored UNCONFIRMED (not yet enforced -- plain Login still works); ConfirmTotp proves the app is in sync, enforces the factor, and hands back one-time recovery codes. From then on a plain Login is refused for that user and LoginTwoFactor is the only door. The factor is stzTotp; per-user state (secret + recovery-code hashes) lives in the store. whether a user has a CONFIRMED (enforced) second factor.

methods.name: EnableTotp
methods.description: begin enrollment: mint a secret, store it UNCONFIRMED, and return [ :secret, :uri ]. Render :uri as a QR code for the user's app; :secret is the same key for manual entry. Nothing is enforced until ConfirmTotp. Raises if a CONFIRMED factor already exists (disable it first); a still-pending enrollment is simply replaced.

methods.name: ConfirmTotp
methods.description: finish enrollment: verify the app's current code. On success the factor is confirmed (now enforced) and a fresh set of one-time recovery codes is returned -- show them to the user ONCE (only their hashes are stored). Returns [] on a bad code (enrollment stays pending).

methods.name: VerifyTotp
methods.description: verify a TOTP code (or a one-time recovery code) for a confirmed user.

methods.name: DisableTotp
methods.description: turn 2FA off (removes the secret + every recovery code).

methods.name: RegenerateRecoveryCodes
methods.description: issue a FRESH set of recovery codes (the old set stops working). Returns the plaintext to show once. Only for a confirmed factor.

methods.name: RecoveryCodesRemaining
methods.description: how many unused recovery codes remain.

methods.name: RequestMagicLink
methods.description: Send a one-time sign-in LINK to the user's email. The emailed token is random (256-bit); only its sha256 is stored, so a leaked store never yields a usable link. ENUMERATION-SAFE: the call behaves identically whether or not the email has an account -- a link is minted and sent only for a real user, but the return is always the same. Requires a bound mail port.

methods.name: RedeemMagicLink
methods.description: redeem a magic-link token -> a session token ("" if invalid / expired / for a user who since vanished, or whose 2FA forbids the shortcut).

methods.name: SetPasswordResetTTL
methods.description: The recovery path is where accounts are taken over, so it holds the same line as every other door: - ENUMERATION-SAFE: the request answers the same whether or not the email has an account; a link is minted and mailed only for a real one; - the token is 256 random bits, stored ONLY as its sha256, ONE-TIME and short-lived (30 min); a newer request cancels the older link; - a reset stores an Argon2id hash and ENDS EVERY SESSION -- an attacker holding one is signed out with the rest; - it does NOT sign anybody in: the next login still asks for the second factor when 2FA is on; - it cannot undo CONTAINMENT: an account a responder or an operator locked (LockAccount) is refused; a lockout from failed attempts, which is what a forgotten password produces, is cleared.

methods.name: ResetPassword
methods.description: Redeem a reset link. 1 when the password was changed, 0 otherwise -- unknown, used, expired, a new password too short, or a locked account.

methods.name: RequestEmailOtp
methods.description: Email a short numeric code (6 digits) the user types back. The code is salted- hashed at rest and one pending code exists per email (a new request replaces it). A wrong code counts toward the brute-force lockout. Enumeration-safe, and requires a bound mail port.

methods.name: VerifyEmailOtp
methods.description: verify an emailed OTP -> a session token ("" on any failure / lockout / a 2FA user).

methods.name: DefineRole
methods.description: The payoff of the whole auth story. A successful login produces not just a session but the ACTOR the governance system already reasons about: a stzSystemActor carrying a capability set (the effectful / sensing / compute / inference lattice) derived from the user's roles, at a trust posture. The SAME username is the governance actor (stzGovernance.MayProceed) and the org-chart person (separation-of-duties). Roles are DEFINED here (capability bundles, app config) and GRANTED per user (durable). Four roles ship by default; an 'assistant' (LLM-backed) role holds only 'inference', so its session is authenticated yet cannot cause effects -- the agentic-safety invariant, extended to identity. define a role = a capability bundle. kinds are drawn from the lattice (effectful / sensing / compute / inference); posture is trusted / external / sandboxed. Re-defining a role replaces it. Returns This.

methods.name: GrantRole
methods.description: grant a role to a user (durable). The role must be defined and the user must exist. Returns This.

methods.name: ActorForUser
methods.description: the ACTOR a user resolves to: a stzSystemActor named for the user, holding the UNION of its roles' capability kinds, at the MOST RESTRICTIVE posture among them. A user with no roles is a capability-less, sandboxed actor -- properly authenticated, yet permitted nothing (least privilege by default).

methods.name: ActorOf
methods.description: the actor behind a LIVE session (NULL if the session is invalid / expired).

methods.name: SessionCan
methods.description: does the logged-in user hold a capability kind? (FALSE for an invalid session.)

methods.name: SessionIsEffectful
methods.description: can this session cause EFFECTS? An assistant/LLM-role session holds only 'inference', so it is authenticated yet effect-less.

methods.name: SessionMayProceed
methods.description: a session-gated governance decision: the session must be LIVE and the governance instance (passed by reference, never held) must permit the action for this user. Bridges authn to the existing authz engine.

methods.name: SetSamlServiceProvider
methods.description: The enterprise counterpart to OIDC: the corporate IdP authenticates the employee and POSTs back a signed assertion; stzAuth verifies it (engine-side XML-DSig, then issuer / audience / validity / replay -- see stzSamlServiceProvider) and opens a normal session. As with OIDC, the user that comes out is an ordinary Softanza citizen with the same governance actor -- SSO is a way IN, not a separate kind of account.

methods.name: SamlUserNameFor
methods.description: the local user name a SAML subject maps to (its NameID -- typically the corporate email).

methods.name: SetPasskeyRelyingParty
methods.description: A passkey replaces the password with a key pair the user's DEVICE holds: the private half never leaves the authenticator, so there is nothing to phish, reuse, or steal in a breach. Registration stores the public key; login is a signature over a fresh challenge. The relying-party judgement (origin, challenge, user presence, the cloned-authenticator counter) lives in stzPasskeyServer; the credentials live in the store, one row per DEVICE. bind the relying party: the domain credentials are bound to, and the exact origin the browser reports. The origin check is what makes a passkey unphishable, so both are required.

methods.name: NewPasskeyChallenge
methods.description: a fresh challenge for either ceremony -- the app holds it for that one exchange, which is what stops a captured response being replayed.

methods.name: RegisterPasskey
methods.description: enroll a device for a user. TRUE on success (PasskeyWhy explains a refusal).

methods.name: PasskeysOf
methods.description: the devices a user has enrolled (public data only -- never a private key).

methods.name: RemovePasskey
methods.description: un-enroll one device (losing a key should not cost the account).

methods.name: LoginWithPasskey
methods.description: sign in with a device -> a session token, or "" (PasskeyWhy explains).

methods.name: LoginWithPasskeyAt
methods.signature: LoginWithPasskeyAt(pcCredId, pcAuthDataB64, pcClientDataB64, pcSigB64, pcExpectedChallenge, pnNow)

methods.name: LoginWithPasskeyWithAt
methods.signature: LoginWithPasskeyWithAt(pcCredId, pcAuthDataB64, pcClientDataB64, pcSigB64, pcExpectedChallenge, pcIp, pcUserAgent, pnNow)

methods.name: SetOidcClient
methods.description: "Sign in with Google / Okta / Entra". The provider proves who the user is and hands back an id-token; stzAuth VERIFIES it locally (signature against the provider's published key, then issuer / audience / expiry / nonce -- see stzOidcClient) and, only then, opens a normal Softanza session. From that point the user is indistinguishable from any other: the same session, the same roles, the same governance ACTOR (phase 5). An external identity is a way IN, not a separate kind of citizen.

methods.name: SetOidcAutoProvision
methods.description: create a local account the first time an external identity signs in (the usual want). Turn it off to admit only pre-provisioned users.

methods.name: OidcWhy
methods.description: why the last external login was refused ("" when it succeeded).

methods.name: OidcUserNameFor

methods.name: LoginWithOidcWithAt
methods.description: > a session token, or "" (with OidcWhy() explaining).

methods.name: IsLockedOut
methods.description: lockout queries

methods.name: LockAccount
methods.description: The failure lockout above is a COUNTER: it engages after N bad passwords and expires by itself. A LOCK is an ACT: a responder or an operator closes the account until someone opens it again. It refuses every login path (they all ask IsLockedOutAt) AND every existing session -- UserOfSession answers "" for a locked user -- and it is kept in the store, so it survives a restart with a durable store.

methods.name: AccountLock
methods.description: [ :reason, :at ] or [] -- why and since when the account is locked.

methods.name: init
methods.description: pcPath = a file path (durable) or ":memory:" (a real sqlite, but process- local). The tables are created on first use.

methods.name: PutUser
methods.description: Every statement below BINDS its values (stzDatabase.ExecWith/RowsWith): a value is never spliced into the SQL text, so none needs escaping and none can change what a statement says. They used to be ~49 strings built by concatenation through a hand-written quote-doubler, _Esc().

methods.description: sessions

methods.name: PutTotp
methods.description: Recovery-code hashes are stored comma-joined in one TEXT column -- a hash is "salt:hash" (hex only), so a comma can never occur inside one.

methods.name: PutChallenge
methods.description: passwordless challenges (magic-link / email-OTP)

methods.name: PutPasskey
methods.description: passkeys (WebAuthn credentials)
methods.signature: PutPasskey(pcCredId, pcUser, pcKty, pcK1, pcK2, pnCount)

methods.name: PutLock
methods.description: administrative locks (containment)

methods.name: GrantRole
methods.description: authz roles (the authn->authz bridge)

methods.name: PutLock
methods.description: A lock is an ACT, not a counter: it stays until someone unlocks it, unlike the failure lockout stzAuth keeps in memory and lets expire.

methods.name: LockOf

methods.name: PutUser

methods.name: PutSession
methods.description: A session is a RECORD: [ :token, :user, :expires, :created, :ip, :ua, :lastseen ] -- so a "your devices" view can list them, and idle timeout has a lastseen to compare. paRec (to PutSession) carries everything but :token.

methods.name: Session

methods.name: TouchSession
methods.description: update a session's last-seen stamp (idle-timeout sliding window). Rebuilds the row rather than mutating a hashlist field in place (that INSERTS a key).

methods.name: Sessions
methods.description: all session records -- for purge / enumeration.

methods.name: SessionsOf
methods.description: the records belonging to one user.

methods.name: PutTotp
methods.description: One row per user with 2FA: the base32 secret, a confirmed flag (a secret is stored unconfirmed at enrollment and only enforced once the user proves a first code), and the list of one-time recovery-code HASHES (never plaintext).

methods.name: PutChallenge
methods.description: A short-lived, one-time challenge. handle = the lookup key (for magic-link, sha256 of the emailed token so the raw token is never stored; for email-OTP, "otp:"+email so a new request replaces the pending one). codehash is empty for magic-link (the token IS the secret) and a salted hash of the code for OTP.

methods.name: GrantRole
methods.description: Per-user role GRANTS (durable). The role DEFINITIONS -- what capabilities a role carries -- are app config held by stzAuth, not stored here.

methods.name: PutPasskey
methods.description: One row per CREDENTIAL, keyed by its id: a user may enroll several devices, and each carries its own public key and signature counter.
methods.signature: PutPasskey(pcCredId, pcUser, pcKty, pcK1, pcK2, pnCount)

methods.name: LockAccount
methods.description: The account is closed: every login path and every live session refuse.

methods.name: RevokeSession
methods.description: The plan targets an ACTOR, so every session of that user ends.

methods.name: RotateSecret
methods.description: Not this responder's to perform: authentication owns accounts and sessions, nothing else. A plan that proposes these needs another responder -- refused loudly, never pretended.

Of graphviz's 24 node shapes, twenty are a circle, a rect or a polygon -- all already here -- and the remaining four (ellipse, egg, cylinder, doublecircle) all need this one. methods.description: paVerts is flat -- x, y, r, g, b, a per vertex, pixel space, channels 0..255. paIndices is 0-based triangle indices into it. Both tiers carry it: the GPU draws the triangles through the ordinary shape pipeline (no new shader, no extra draw call), and ToSVG() emits one <polygon> per triangle -- exact for flat-coloured UI geometry, an approximation for a gradient mesh, where the GPU interpolates and SVG cannot.

methods.name: AddJustifiedText

methods.name: ToPNG
methods.description: Four is the knee and the rest is a bad trade: five through seven buy 1.3% for another 2.4 ms, and nine spends 5.1x the time of one to beat four by 4%. So four is the default and the dial is exposed, because a caller writing one file for a page and a caller writing nine hundred for a test suite are not answering the same question.

methods.name: ToPNGHiRes
methods.description: 4x MSAA antialiases a shape's edges and still beads a thin near-axis line light and dark along its length: its four samples are fixed, so a half-pixel diagonal catches them unevenly. Rendering at 2x gives sixteen effective samples where the line is and the bead fills in. It is not the default -- a test that compares rendered bytes wants the plain render, and a nine-hundred-file suite does not want to pay 4x the fill -- so a FIGURE meant to be shown asks for it and a check does not. Two is the knee; three and four are for print.

methods.name: ToPixels
methods.description: Raw RGBA8 bytes of the GPU tier, for a caller that wants the pixels themselves (comparisons, compositing, tests).

methods.name: ToPixelsHiRes
methods.description: ...and the supersampled pixels, box-averaged down: what ToPNGHiRes writes, for a caller that wants the bytes rather than a file.

methods.name: Flush
methods.description: AND A CALLER CLOSING A GROUP OF SHAPES, which is the second reason and was found the hard way. SetFont, Fill and Stroke are deliberately RETROACTIVE on a pending shape -- that is what makes AddTextQ(..).Fill(..) work -- so the LAST shape of a group stays open until something else is added. A label engine drew ninety-six names and then wrote a caption at another size, and the caption resized the ninety-sixth name. Flush() is how a group is closed on purpose.

methods.name: Resize
methods.description: Empty the display list, keeping the background and the GPU buffers. What an ANIMATED canvas calls at the top of each frame -- without it the list grows by a frame's worth of shapes forever. Change the canvas's extents. The engine scene and this face are resized by the SAME call, so Width()/Height() cannot drift from what is actually being drawn -- which they did, silently, the first time a window retargeted a canvas: the face kept answering its construction size while the scene had moved on.

methods.name: SetGoal
methods.description: THE GOAL: one contract, accepted explicitly, then MONITORED -------- A conversation has exactly ONE goal. It is not assembled from inside the session -- it is BUILT as a stzGoal and HANDED OVER; from then on the conversation is accountable for it and watches it until it is FULFILLED (no gaps left in the space) or REVOKED (abandoned, with a reason). No goal = no loop: the elicitation is goal-driven, so asking without one REFUSES rather than inventing something to ask (LAW 3).

methods.name: init
methods.description: The course's facts are the CORE's course.zknw plus, when an overlay is laid on, the overlay's own courses/<slug>/course.zknw -- MERGED, never shadowed: an overlay adds a chapter or attaches an exercise to a chapter without copying the core manifest (charter 4.1).

methods.name: CurriculumFacts
methods.description: the curriculum: the PLAN of the course, against which what SHIPS (course.zknw) is measured. It carries plans-chapter-NN, trains and requires; course.zknw carries only what exists.

methods.name: UnwrittenChapterIds
methods.description: Planned chapters with no text yet -- printed by name, never summed into the shipped count.

methods.name: Prerequisites
methods.description: Everything a chapter needs first, walked to the root; a cycle raises.

methods.name: ChapterIds
methods.description: Chapter ids in course order (the order lives in the relation name, has-chapter-NN, because .zknw has no ordered list -- charter 5.2).

methods.name: ChapterQ
methods.description: A chapter with no text in a language is a RED fact, never a quiet fallback to English (law 7).

methods.name: NamesTaughtBy
methods.description: what each chapter teaches, read from its own cells (the tutor's rule 2) The names a chapter's cells call, from its English edition: the cells are identical in every edition, only the prose moves.

methods.name: TeachesWhere
methods.description: The first chapter, in course order, whose cells call a name; "" when no chapter does. Case does not matter.

methods.name: TitleOf
methods.description: The title of a chapter in a language, from that edition's first line.

methods.name: RunChapterQ
methods.description: Runs every cell of a chapter in one fresh process, over the world the program (or its overlay) supplies, then observes where each cell can run. The chapter object comes back holding both.

methods.name: RunChapterInQ
methods.description: The chapter in several languages: each language in its OWN fresh process (no cell can lean on another language's variables), the processes side by side. Returns the chapters, run and observed.

methods.name: Complete
methods.description: domain-valid continuations (the constrained-grammar spirit): an entity completes with its relations; a relation with its objects; a fragment with matching entities

methods.name: GenerateCorpus
methods.description: every fact rendered as a sentence -- RUNG 2's teacher-free training corpus (correct by construction: these ARE the facts)

methods.name: Tokenizer
methods.description: R4 step 8 -- the word-level DOMAIN TOKENIZER: a closed domain earns a closed vocabulary (id 1 = <unk>, then entities, types, relations, and every corpus word). The neural rung trains over these ids; the deterministic rung already speaks them.

methods.name: TrainNeuralRung
methods.description: RUNG 2: the NEURAL domain LM ----------------------------------------- A neural BIGRAM language model: one-hot(current token) -> softmax over the domain vocabulary -> next token. Trained ONLY on GenerateCorpus() (sentences correct-by-construction), no remote teacher -- the whole point of the Foundry: a project's own knowledge becomes a model that GENERATES domain text. Rung 1 (deterministic Ask/Complete) still owns truth; this rung learns the corpus's word-transition distribution. The softmax + categorical-cross-entropy floor makes it possible.

methods.name: NextToken
methods.description: the token (string) the neural rung predicts to follow a word

methods.name: NextTokenConfidence
methods.description: the neural rung's confidence in its predicted next token (a real probability -- softmax normalizes over the whole vocabulary)

methods.name: NeuralGenerate
methods.description: greedy generation: a seed word + nSteps neural next-tokens

methods.name: TrainingSetQ
methods.description: THE HELD SET IS LIVE THROUGH HERE. Haro COPIES an object into an attribute, so the set handed to the constructor is a SNAPSHOT: growing the caller's own object afterwards would NOT reach this learner. Grow it through this accessor -- oLearner.TrainingSetQ().AddExample(...) -- which reaches the real held set (accessor + method call is live in Haro).

methods.name: Train
methods.description: Third time this phase has found this shape: the CSV module's per-cell regex recompile, the linear solver's per-variable re-parse, and now this. The expensive line is rarely the one the plan names -- the plan said "trees -> engine", and the tree was never the problem.

methods.name: ToGraph
methods.description: the learned model as a REAL stzGraph: decision nodes + labeled value edges + leaf nodes -- queryable like any other graph

methods.name: SeedProposal
methods.description: The offline door, and it is a METHOD rather than something a caller does through FunctionQ(): Haro copies an object on assignment, so `oF = oAg.FunctionQ()` then `oF.SeedAnswer(...)` seeds a copy the agent will never read. Seeding from inside the class writes the agent's own function, which is the only version that ticks.

methods.name: FunctionQ
methods.description: The live function, so a caller can seed it, fake it or read its budget BEFORE the agent is handed to a host. After the handoff the host's copy is the one that ticks -- the same rule stzAgentHost already states for every supervised agent.

methods.name: Cycle
methods.description: ONE TICK. Returns 1 when a proposal was made AND validated, 0 otherwise -- and 0 always says why rather than passing for quiet.

methods.name: Apply
methods.description: Same [ :ran, :verified, :why ] contract as the closure-built skill, so stzPIAgent.Cycle() cannot tell the two apart -- which is the point of a front-end.

methods.name: Log
methods.description: the structured log of the delivery's phases (Deploy). Queryable + renderable: oDelivery.Log().AsJson(), oDelivery.Log().EntriesOfLevel(:error).

methods.name: SetAppTopology
methods.description: attach the solution's application model -- named datasets + per-part roles. The emulator renders each part FROM it (its real menu / computed dashboard), instead of a shared placeholder.

methods.name: NeedsIn
methods.description: declare the Softanza capabilities a part's code uses (:PivotTable, :Unicode, ...). Stored as lowercased keys (the canonical form).

methods.name: UseServices
methods.description: ONE CAVEAT, and it is Haro's, not this method's: an attribute store COPIES (probed -- bind a service on your own handle afterwards and this delivery will not see it). So either finish configuring the registry BEFORE attaching it, or make later changes THROUGH the accessor, which reaches the stored object: oDelivery.ServicesQ().BindLiveQ(:payments, oImpl, "stripe_key").

methods.name: NeedsServiceIn
methods.description: Which external services a part's code actually calls. The parallel of NeedsIn (Softanza capabilities); this is the OUTSIDE world.

methods.name: ExternalDependencies
methods.description: The rehearsed surface, one record per service: [ :service, :posture, :secret, :bound, :parts ] This is the answer to "what does shipping this actually require of me?", available before a single byte is built.

methods.name: ProductionCredentials
methods.description: The credentials a production deploy will require -- names only, never values.

methods.name: ServiceFindingsForProduction
methods.description: REHEARSE THE GATE. The registry only reports sandbox-in-production once its phase IS production, so a pre-flight check asks the question in that frame and then puts the phase back -- you learn what shipping would say without declaring that you are shipping. (The plane's own habit: rehearse, then commit.)

methods.name: AsRuleGraph
methods.description: Project parts AND services into one graph, so a rule can ask the question neither side can answer alone: does a part that is BOUND TO A SITE (i.e. destined for production) depend on a service that is still a fake? See stzServiceRuleSet.

methods.name: InferNeedsIn
methods.description: a first inference: scan the app source for capability markers -> keys. Upgradeable to the stzCodeGraph call-edge analysis (lexical starting point).

methods.name: DeployTo
methods.description: WHERE each part deploys in production: bind a target site to the part it hosts. Site-first, part-second -- demystified: "deploy to <site>, the <part>". (Deploy(:Emulated) needs no sites -- it runs in the browser; production does.)

methods.name: SetActor
methods.description: the executing actor -- governs whether Deploy(:Production) COMMITS or only rehearses (only an effectful actor may cross the governed bridge to reality).

methods.name: RequiresIn
methods.description: what a part NEEDS from its host: memory / compute / storage (a stzResourceSpec). Parallels NeedsIn (capabilities); here it is the physical footprint the target must provide -- the CI/IaC "resources.requests" idea.

methods.name: ShipBundle
methods.description: ship an emulator's bundle DIRECTORY as a part's production artifact. The bundle you built and debugged with Deploy(:Emulated) becomes what Deploy(:Production) ships -- the same tree, one directive. pBundle is a stzEmulator or a dir path.

methods.name: ShipSlice
methods.description: ship only pcPart's SLICE of the bundle -- its app (index.html) + engine subset (stz_<part>.wasm) + the bridge (stz.js), not the whole mission-control. A frontend deploys only what it needs to run.

methods.name: Plan
methods.description: REHEARSE the placement & scope plan -- no bytes built. This is Build()'s thinking made visible (VSF rehearse->plan->commit).

methods.name: Deploy
methods.description: Deploy() covers BOTH phases (Scope-Oriented: the deploy scope is the frame). :Emulated   -> the programming phase: generate the web-based mission-control emulator (via stzEmulator) where the whole solution runs and is debugged visually, part by part. :Production  -> the same parts cross the governed bridge to real target SITES. Deploy(:Production) DRIVES a stzDeployment: it binds each part to its site (from DeployTo) and, IF the actor may commit (effectful), STORES + LAUNCHES it -- otherwise it returns the deployment as a rehearsal. Emulation rehearses in the browser; production commits.

methods.name: KeyMaterial
methods.description: the key material (governed).

methods.name: Log
methods.description: the structured log of the deployment run -- queryable and renderable (oDep.Log().EntriesOfLevel(:error), oDep.Log().AsJson()). Populated by Run().

methods.name: SetTarget
methods.description: bind a part to its target site. For many at once, use SetTargets.

methods.name: RunAfter
methods.description: order the plan: pcPart runs AFTER pcDependsOn is verified (a plan-DAG edge). Simple deployments declare none; complex ones (a frontend after its backend) do.

methods.name: Artifact
methods.description: attach a REAL build output to ship for a part (the per-part stz_<part>.wasm, the app bundle, the native binary...). pcRelName is its name at the destination; pcPath is the built file on disk. Shipped byte-for-byte alongside the manifest.

methods.name: AttachBundle
methods.description: wire an emulator's built bundle DIRECTORY straight in as a part's production artifact -- the SAME tree you emulated becomes what ships. Accepts a stzEmulator (built on demand) or a bundle directory path; the bundle lands under the solution name.

methods.name: AttachSlice
methods.description: ship a part's OWN slice from an emulator bundle -- its app (as index.html), its engine subset (stz_<part>.wasm), and the bridge (stz.js) -- NOT the whole mission-control. A frontend part deploys only what it needs to run.

methods.name: MayCommit
methods.description: the governance gate: may this deployment cross to reality?

methods.name: Plan
methods.description: the deployment plan (rehearsal) -------------------- each part -> [ part, kind, target, siteName, siteKind, protocol ]

methods.name: Store
methods.description: perform (governed) --------------------------------- store each part's deploy artifact on its bound site. returns [ committed(0/1), [ [part, site, outcome], ... ] ]

methods.name: Steps
methods.description: the plan of steps (order, gates, rollback) --------- the deployment PLAN as ordered steps. A simple deployment is the default chain per part -- provision? -> store -> launch -> verify; After() edges add cross-part ordering (a frontend after its backend). Returns [ [name, op, part, siteName, [needs]], ... ], topologically ordered so every dependency precedes its dependants.

methods.name: WasRun
methods.description: EXECUTE the ordered plan (governed). Each step runs its op; the verify step is a GATE (the site must be launched). On any failure, the completed store/launch steps are ROLLED BACK in reverse -- the deployment is transactional. Returns [ committed(0/1), [ [stepName, outcome], ... ] ]. No effectful actor -> rehearse. Did Run() execute at all? A deployment REFUSED upstream -- by the service gate in stzDelivery, say -- comes back untouched, and "nothing happened" is then assertable without reading the log.

methods.name: WasCommitted
methods.description: Did it commit, or only rehearse? Rehearsed steps touch nothing.

methods.name: Feasibility
methods.description: feasibility (host resources) ----------------------- Per-site admission check: sum the requirements of the parts bound to each site and test the site's capacity (or its ability to PROVISION one). Returns [ [siteName, requiredText, capacityText, fits(0/1), note], ... ]. This is the same "does the host have room?" question a K8s scheduler / CI runner answers.

methods.name: Feasible
methods.description: TRUE only if every site can host its parts (fits or can provision).

methods.name: SetKind
methods.description: the access config (Q-fluent: chainable via the ...Q suffix)

methods.name: SetAuthRef
methods.description: auth is EITHER a plain reference string (e.g. "env/DEPLOY_KEY", back-compat) OR a stzSecret. When it is a secret, the site stores the OBJECT and displays only its redacted descriptor -- the key never lands in Config/ConfigJson.

methods.name: SetAuthFromStore
methods.description: reference the auth secret BY NAME from a central stzSecretStore. The site holds NO key and NO store object -- only the name (Haro copies objects on assignment, so a held store would be a private copy whose audit no one sees). The reveal is done through the SHARED store, passed by reference at reveal time (ResolveAuthVia), so the store's gate applies AND the store audits it. This is how a project keeps ONE complete audit trail across every reveal.

methods.name: SetCapacity
methods.description: what the host PROVIDES (its capacity). For a real host it is discovered via the provider API; for a fixed host it is declared here.

methods.name: SetProvider
methods.description: name a provisioning provider -> this host can be CREATED/resized to meet a requirement (IaC-style), not just deployed to.

methods.name: Name
methods.description: reads

methods.name: HasSecretAuth
methods.description: the site holds a secret (directly, or by name in a store) rather than a ref.

methods.name: ResolveAuth
methods.description: the LIVE auth value -- GOVERNED. For a directly-held stzSecret it reveals with the actor gate; for a plain ref string it returns it as-is. A STORE-BACKED secret cannot be revealed here -- the store must be passed by reference so its audit is real; use ResolveAuthVia(store, actor).

methods.name: ResolveAuthVia
methods.description: the store-aware reveal: the shared store is passed HERE (by reference), so its gate applies AND it AUDITS the access -- the project's one audit trail stays complete. For a non-store-backed site the store is ignored and this behaves like ResolveAuth(actor).

methods.name: Config
methods.description: the access config as inspectable DATA -- the LINK between the programming environment and this site (connection + storage + control). CAPACITY AND PROVIDER BELONG HERE. They are exactly what _SiteFeasibility() reads to decide whether a part fits a site or has to be provisioned -- and they appeared in NONE of the three renderings below. A site could be declared, printed and saved without the two facts that decide whether the deployment is possible, and a reloaded site would report "capacity not declared -- assumed ok", turning a SHORTFALL into a pass.

methods.name: ConfigJson
methods.description: the config, serialized -- so a target site can be SAVED, versioned, shared: the persistent link the dev/emulation environment reads to reach a site.

methods.name: Reachable
methods.description: A live backend turns the site config into a REAL command run through the managed child (SpawnProcess) -- the same path stzBuilder uses to run zig. The commands are rehearsable (Commands() shows them before anything runs). :LocalRepo uses direct file ops; :GitRepo runs real git (proven end to end against a local bare repo); :Server runs scp/ssh; a scriptable host provisions via its provider CLI. The commands are correct wherever the tool + target exist -- in this sandbox git and the local repo complete; scp/ssh/docker/aws are generated and run through the same child, but need a real host/registry/account to finish.

methods.name: Provision
methods.description: provision a scriptable host to meet a requirement (the IaC move -- bring the host into existence, don't just deploy to it). Runs the provider CLI via the child.

methods.name: Commands
methods.description: the real commands, rehearsable (see them before they run)

methods.name: WhenKind
methods.description: declaring

methods.name: Repeats
methods.description: BURST: n of them...

methods.name: Within
methods.description: ...inside this window (ms of wall time).

methods.name: PerActor
methods.description: count per actor rather than across all actors -- credential stuffing is per account, not per installation.

methods.name: ThenKind
methods.description: SEQUENCE: this kind must follow the watched one.

methods.name: OnAnyOccurrence
methods.description: ANY: one occurrence is already the story.

methods.name: Unusual
methods.description: UNUSUAL: the newest window against the kind's own history.

methods.name: Corroborated
methods.description: The corroboration law: no error-severity alarm on a single signal -- one anomalous read is a rumor.

methods.name: CheckAgainst
methods.description: judging ----------------------------------------------------- Judge a ledger. Returns findings in the unified rule shape -- hand them to stzRuleReport.Ingest().

methods.name: Explain
methods.description: legibility

methods.name: CheckAgainst
methods.description: Judge a ledger with every detection; findings in the unified shape, ready for stzRuleReport.Ingest().

methods.name: FiredNames
methods.description: The names that fired, in order (what an incident is opened from).

methods.name: SetLayout
methods.description: A LAYOUT NAME THIS DOES NOT KNOW IS REFUSED, not stored. It used to take anything, and an unrecognised name became top-down in silence -- so `SetLayout(:LeftToRight)` drew a top-down picture and there was nothing anywhere to say the instruction had been dropped. A setter that accepts a value it will not honour is worse than one that refuses: the caller has evidence of neither.

methods.name: SetFocusColor
methods.description: The focus colour's setter, missing until now. ExportToStyl() has always WRITTEN a focus section (color + penwidth), and _ApplyStyle() has always called This.SetFocusColor() to read it back -- a method nobody had written, so loading any exported .stzstyl died on R14. Same shape as its siblings: resolve the name, keep the resolved value.

methods.name: Fact
methods.description: CATMULL-ROM through the bends rather than a polyline: the bends are where the edge must BE, not where it must turn a corner, and a curve reading smoothly past a box is what distinguishes a routed edge from a dog-leg. Ortho keeps its corners -- that is the point of ortho. -- WHAT THIS PICTURE CAN ANSWER (DN9b) -------------------------------- The same verb the math plane answers, over the things a notation picture holds: its nodes, its edges, where the renderer put them, and the verdicts its own governance reaches. A kind this plane cannot answer is refused by name rather than answered with a zero.

methods.name: Rendition
methods.description: A VALUE THAT SAYS WHAT IT IS (DN9g) --------------------------------- NOTE THE NAME. This class already has a Display(), and it does not return anything: it writes Graphviz source and opens a viewer. Six such methods exist under base/, and they already mean two incompatible things -- three print, three launch. That is why the returning verb is called Rendition() here, and why the display contract cannot take the name Display() without first deciding which of its two existing meanings to break.

methods.name: OnPress
methods.description: A DRAG IS ONE UNDO, not one per pointer-move. The cell follows the cursor by pinning directly -- the picture has to keep up -- and the COMMAND is issued once, at release, from the position the cell held when the drag began. Otherwise a single drag would leave a hundred entries in the log and an undo would move the cell one pixel.

methods.name: OnMove
methods.description: So a move records where the pointer is and nothing else. The window draws the scene it already has and puts the dragged cell on top of it -- DragPreview() says where -- and the layout runs ONCE, at release, when the author has decided. The model is untouched until then, which is also why an abandoned drag leaves nothing behind: there was nothing to undo.

methods.name: OnCancel

methods.name: UiRewire

methods.name: ToSoundOf
methods.description: what a meaning sounds like (no device needed) ----------------------- The motif as DATA. Works with no audio hardware, which is what lets a CI machine assert the vocabulary.

methods.name: IsSilentValue
methods.description: Muted is the one value whose rendering is nothing. Asking is legitimate.

methods.name: SetAmbientFloor
methods.description: Colour's doctrine, transposed: a sound system that cannot fail an audibility check does not have one. The check is a MARGIN over the floor.

methods.name: MarginMetric
methods.description: The margin now uses LoudnessOfSupport: the SAME K-weighting and the same -0.691 + 10log10(z) formula, over the sound's own length. It is not a standard LUFS figure and the metric name says so -- but it is the ear's own weighting rather than a flat average, which is the difference between a gate that models hearing and one that models arithmetic.

methods.name: RequiredMarginOf
methods.description: The gate. A cue needs 10 LU of headroom over the room; an alert needs 20.

methods.name: WouldFireAt
methods.description: THE DECISION IS A PURE FUNCTION of (state, meaning, now), so a guard can assert the contract on a machine with no audio device at all. Fire() calls exactly this, with the transport's clock.

methods.name: RecordFireAt
methods.description: The state advance, separated from the decision so both the real path and a device-less guard drive the same code.

methods.name: Start
methods.description: hearing it

methods.name: SetDuckDepth
methods.description: SS3: ducking -------------------------------------------------------- How deep, in dB. Declared, never inferred -- a caller who wants a different depth argues with a number.

methods.name: DucksApplied
methods.description: COUNTED, like everything else this plane does behind a listener's back. "Why did that get quiet" must have an answer that is a number.

methods.name: GainOf
methods.description: The gain the RENDER is applying to a value's bus right now. During a ramp this is somewhere between the old value and the target, which is what lets a guard prove the ramp MOVES rather than jumps.

methods.name: DuckUnder
methods.description: Duck every value QUIETER IN MEANING than this one, and leave the rest alone. Ramped, so it cannot click.

methods.name: Unduck
methods.description: Everything back to unity, on the same ramp. Restoring with a JUMP would click exactly as ducking with one would.

methods.name: SetVoiceLanguage
methods.description: VC4: SAY -- the earcon, then the phrase that says WHICH ------------- Which language the phrase is spoken in. REFUSED rather than substituted if the machine has no voice for it -- speaking French to an operator who asked for English is worse than saying nothing.

methods.name: VoiceLanguage
methods.description: Which language it is actually speaking -- empty until one is set and ACCEPTED, so a caller can tell "not asked yet" from "asked and refused".

methods.name: ToSoundOfSaying
methods.description: Needs no audio device, which is what lets a guard measure the composition on a machine that cannot play it.

methods.name: Say
methods.description: Say it: the earcon, then the phrase. Queued, not played immediately -- call TickSpeech() (or SpeakQueueToEnd()) to advance.

methods.name: TickSpeech
methods.description: One step. Starts the next phrase when nothing is speaking, and reaps the transport when it ends. Cheap; call it as often as you like.

methods.name: SpeakQueueToEnd
methods.description: This method OCCUPIES THE THREAD. Nothing can call Say while it runs, so the queue it starts with is the queue it finishes with: there is nothing left to cancel, and rendering the whole of it into one buffer is not a loss of behaviour, only of churn. TickSpeech keeps the per-phrase transport precisely because a program that ticks CAN be interrupted, and there the ability to stop mid-sentence is the point.

methods.name: SpeechGapSeconds
methods.description: The silence between a cue and its phrase, and between two announcements when a queue drains as one. Exposed because a guard has to be able to account for it rather than assume it.

methods.name: TriggerToEarMs
methods.description: What a caller must not assume. Haro occupancy plus the measured device and OS floor -- see plan S.5 for where each number comes from.

methods.name: CanAcknowledgeWithin
methods.description: Rule 18 allows 100 ms. This answers whether a sound can be the acknowledgement, and on this pipeline the answer is no.

methods.name: AddWorldPage
methods.description: A world's page: the same article as a chapter, listed in the language's menu under "World" rather than a number, after the chapters of that language.

methods.name: Channel
methods.description: stateless: the bus lives in the engine (process-global channels) Declare (idempotently) a channel. Returns This for chaining.

methods.name: Subscribe
methods.description: Subscribe to a channel (auto-declares it). Returns a subscriber id (>0) or a negative error.

methods.description: Emit a payload on a channel (auto-declares it). Returns how many subscribers it was delivered to.

methods.name: EventCount
methods.description: It rises and never falls WHILE THE CHANNEL LIVES, which is not the same as monotonic, and the difference bites. DestroyChannel and ClearAll below put a channel back to zero, so a consumer holding a previous count sees a SMALLER number and, if it only tests for "bigger than last time", decides there is no new work -- for good. A DECREASE means the channel is new and the consumer must re-baseline; stzAgentHost.TickDue does exactly that.

methods.name: LastEvent
methods.description: The most recent payload emitted on the channel ("" if none).

methods.name: ChannelGeneration
methods.description: EventCount alone cannot tell a consumer that a channel was remade: the count restarts at zero, and by the time anyone polls it may already have climbed back above the value they remembered, so "did the number go down" misses it. The generation never repeats and never resets, so comparing it is exact rather than a race. stzAgentHost.TickDue re-baselines on it.

A LIST, because a range that crosses a bidi seam is genuinely in several pieces on screen. An empty range selects nothing -- for a caret, ask CaretRectAt.

methods.name: InkOver
methods.description: This used to ask StzIsDarkColor and choose white or the caller's ink, and it put black names on dark blue and dark red -- which the Principal returned twice. The house HAS a contrast contract: StzReadableTextOn(background, sizePx, bold) answers the ink AND whether that size can carry it, measured against WCAG's 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large. A drawing file has no business having its own opinion about contrast when the colour system holds one.

methods.name: PaperBoxOf
methods.description: a region's box ON THE PAPER: what the reader's eye measures a name against, which is not the box it has on the sphere

methods.name: SetInsetInk
methods.description: AN INSET LABELS THE WAY ITS PARENT LABELS ITS UNITS -- names, or the parent's official codes where it has them, and never a sequential number, which would need a second key and a sheet with two keys has given up. If a mark still will not fit at the inset's scale it is REPORTED, and the answer is a larger box, not a cleverer placement.

methods.name: AddInset
methods.description: paWindow is the ground to magnify, [ lon0, lat0, lon1, lat1 ]; paBox is where it goes on the canvas, [ x0, y0, x1, y1 ].

methods.name: InsetHolding
methods.description: the FIRST inset holding it, and not the nearest: two insets over the same ground is a mistake the caller should see, not a tie to break here

methods.name: SetHighlight
methods.description: 1. BORDERS ARE DARK AND THIN, NOT WHITE. A white border between two pale classes erases the boundary exactly where the map is doing its work; a hairline of the ink colour separates them at every shade. Our World in Data, the Financial Times and the Economist all stroke dark, and the reason is legibility at the light end. 2. THE LEGEND IS A RAMP WITH ITS EDGES LABELLED, not a stack of "10 to 20" rows. A reader matches a colour to a position on a bar, and the numbers belong at the JOINS because that is where the meaning changes. It carries a NO-DATA swatch, hatched, so "not measured" is visibly not a value. 3. WHAT IS SELECTED IS OUTLINED, NOT RECOLOURED. Recolouring a selection destroys the one thing the map encodes. A heavy dark outline says "this one" while leaving its class readable. 4. TEXT OVER COLOUR NEEDS A HALO. A white name on a mid-orange is unreadable at every size; the same name with a thin dark halo is readable on every shade in the ramp. This is the colour system's contrast contract solved the way cartographers solve it, since a label on a choropleth has no single background to contrast with. the regions to outline heavily: by name, or by class through HighlightClass below

methods.name: HighlightClass
methods.description: SELECT A WHOLE CLASS, which is what clicking a legend swatch means: "show me everyone between 2 and 5 per cent". The class is outlined on the map AND framed in the legend, so the two read as one gesture.

The diagram plane has had this since DN3b; a map is the surface that wants it most, because a reader's first question of any choropleth is "which country is that and what is its number".

methods.name: DrawNoDataHatchOn
methods.description: The lines are CLIPPED TO THE SHAPE, by the same routine for a country and for the legend's own swatch. The first legend swatch drew its hatching as unclipped diagonals and they ran out of the box on both sides -- "its rectangle in the legend is not correct", which it was not. One clipper, two callers, and no second definition of a hatch.

methods.name: IsUnclassed
methods.description: NO DATA MEANS NO VALUE, and it does not mean "a value my scale has no box for". A country measured at 35 on a scale topping out at 30 is data -- badly classed data, which is the cartographer's problem and not the country's -- and hatching it would tell the reader nobody counted it. So this asks for the VALUE where the map is numeric, and for membership where the map is categorical, since a map cannot be both.
